issues.problem: ctx4 (bully now isolated) and ctx5 (fraudulent company went bankrupt) are trouble people brought on themselves, so 自業自得 (also in the set) fits the braces just as well.

issues.problem: ctx4 (illness → took up marathons) and ctx5 (office worker opened a bakery) read as a fresh start in mood, where 心機一転 fits as well. Story also said the Buddhist resolve was 'often by leaving ordinary life to enter the Buddhist path', a detail I could not stand behind as part of the term's meaning.
issues.action: ctx4 now: shocked by health-check results, resolved and started running every morning; ctx5 now: resolved, went to night pastry school, opened a bakery (stresses a firm resolution to a demanding goal). Story trimmed to the certain part: short for 一念発起菩提心, the moment one resolves to seek enlightenment.

issues.problem: ctx1 (棚の組み立てに…悪戦苦闘した) and ctx3 (設定に悪戦苦闘してる) fit 四苦八苦 (in the set) equally well. The near diff called 四苦八苦 'being in great distress or at a loss', which undersells its modern sense of having great trouble doing something.
issues.action: ctx1 rewritten as 組み立て式の棚と一晩中悪戦苦闘した, ctx3 as 設定と悪戦苦闘中だよ. The と + opponent frame and 〜中 are typical of 悪戦苦闘 and much less natural with 四苦八苦. Near diff rewritten.
